neighbours.label: Event-timeline narration: the token after a dated or 'on the day of' framing that introduces what happened at a scheduled event (On the day of the conference, On May 12, a treaty), vs descriptions of the same events without a timeline frame
fire: Tickets went on sale in May. On the day of the festival, thousands of fans lined the streets.
The board met in January. On the day of the vote, every member was present in the hall.
Applications close on March 5th and the interviews will follow the next week.
Rehearsals ran for a month. On the day of the premiere, the theatre was sold out.
The town planned the parade for weeks. On the day of the parade, it rained heavily.
Voting opens on Monday and the results will follow on Wednesday evening.
Invitations were mailed in spring. On the day of the wedding, the guests arrived by boat.
Training lasted six weeks. On the day of the exam, the candidates waited outside the room.
quiet: Tickets went on sale in May. Most fans prefer the evening concerts on the main stage.
The board met in January. Every member has served at least two terms on the council.
Applications are reviewed by a panel of three teachers from different schools.
Rehearsals ran for a month. The theatre has red seats and a painted ceiling.
The town planned the parade for weeks. Its main street is lined with old oak trees.
Voters in the district are mostly farmers and small business owners.
Invitations were mailed in spring. The guests were mostly old friends from college.
Training lasted six weeks. The candidates came from many different countries.
